learnings.lesson: Constructed response profiles validate policy mechanics but cannot confirm that target-model response heterogeneity exists.
learnings.apply_when: A Phase-2 empirical systems hypothesis uses purpose-built simulator profiles as evidence for a live target claim.

learnings.lesson: Replay-deadline safety requires a calibrated tail/dependence model and an explicit void-risk target; observed maxima or an arbitrary margin are not coverage guarantees.
learnings.apply_when: A Phase-2 or Phase-4 design sizes a returned candidate set against the 9000-second replay deadline.

learnings.lesson: A sufficient-condition decomposition must use independently specified loss bounds; defining the loss from the predicted outcome can reduce the antecedent to the conclusion.
learnings.apply_when: A Phase-2 hypothesis uses an oracle-margin or regret decomposition to justify a metric threshold.

learnings.lesson: When probes are retained and scored, adaptation must be isolated from fixed and nonadaptive comparators, and every screen, validation, discard, fallback and fill cost must be charged in the end-to-end comparison.
learnings.apply_when: A Phase-2 adaptive-policy experiment retains exploratory probes in the evaluated output.

learnings.lesson: A public deterministic seed plus an opened flag is not held-out blinding; use commit-reveal or a post-freeze public randomness beacon with an append-only opening ledger.
learnings.apply_when: A Phase-2/3 synthetic held-out test claims outcomes were unavailable when the protocol was frozen.

learnings.lesson: Uncertainty machinery must match the estimand: fixed finite splits need exact descriptive contrasts, while generator-population bootstrap must include comparator selection or use an independent selection split.
learnings.apply_when: A Phase-2/5 comparison bootstraps performance against a best-on-sample control.

learnings.lesson: A post-freeze randomness protocol must parse provider timestamps canonically and bind clean code, contract, predictions, and ledgers at freeze, reveal, and evaluation; a future pulse alone is not an executable holdout protocol.
learnings.apply_when: A Phase-2/3 held-out design derives outcomes from an external randomness beacon.

learnings.lesson: A directional identity such as per-unit argmax being no worse than a global argmax does not justify a materiality magnitude; the threshold needs an independent bound or must be labeled normative.
learnings.apply_when: A Phase-2 hypothesis sets an effect-size threshold for a deterministic optimization advantage.

learnings.lesson: A finite exact prediction with a materiality threshold is falsified by every outcome below that threshold; positive-but-subthreshold can be a descriptive subtype, not an inconclusive escape hatch.
learnings.apply_when: A Phase-2/5 fixed-finite estimand has no sampling uncertainty and a preregistered minimum effect.

learnings.lesson: Machine-readable protocol prose is still underdetermined unless each state transition has computable predecessors and every enum, sentinel, serialization, nested schema, and ledger update has one value.
learnings.apply_when: A Phase-2 hypothesis claims a held-out protocol is executable from a JSON contract.

learnings.lesson: Pinning a language/runtime version does not pin transcendental math; discontinuous floor decisions need a specific libm/container, correctly rounded functions, or a certified distance from integer boundaries.
learnings.apply_when: A Phase-2/3 generator uses log/exp results inside floor or threshold operations and claims exact reproducibility.

learnings.lesson: Exclusive creation followed by writing is not crash-atomic; terminal artifacts and ledgers require same-directory staged bytes, atomic no-replace publication, directory fsync, and idempotent recovery states.
learnings.apply_when: A Phase-2/3 held-out protocol claims every crash reaches one immutable terminal artifact or ledger resolution.

learnings.lesson: A deterministic calibration ensemble supports a future randomness-derived target only under an explicit seed-domain exchangeability or cryptographic pseudorandomness assumption; unpredictability alone is insufficient.
learnings.apply_when: A Phase-2 prediction uses fixed hash-derived calibration masters to support a future public-randomness master.

learnings.lesson: A novelty-score invariant must use the actual SDK cell-signature representation and hash the file that implements it; a separately defined candidate ID cannot be substituted for a trace-derived score-cell hash.
learnings.apply_when: A Phase-2/3 synthetic evaluator derives a score uniqueness bonus from SDK trace or cell-signature behavior.

learnings.lesson: An externally posted terminal message needs a durable pre-post idempotency key plus read-before-repost and duplicate policy; local atomic files do not close a crash between external post and receipt recording.
learnings.apply_when: A held-out custody protocol claims crash recovery across an external thread or service post.

learnings.lesson: Parseable metric names must satisfy the verifier's exact regex; numeric concepts should be spelled as words when the extractor permits only lowercase letters and underscores.
learnings.apply_when: A Phase-3/4 experiment specification requires stdout metrics extracted by `grep ^[a-z_]*:`.

learnings.lesson: Scientific evidence bundles need a fresh transaction boundary before computation, command-owned logs, COMPLETE-last hash manifests, atomic no-replace publication, and failure tests; internally consistent files alone do not exclude stale mixed outputs.
learnings.apply_when: A reusable experiment runner writes canonical evidence that will be trusted after crashes or retries.

learnings.lesson: Exact attempt identity must be checked lexically before path resolution and symlink following; live/dangling aliases require lexists/lstat, no-follow descriptor reads, and race tests.
learnings.apply_when: A preregistered run identity is part of a completion manifest or one-use execution contract.

learnings.lesson: In the public ORF crossed generator, cliff behavior and reset overhead explain most conditional-regret magnitude, while the novelty constant is negligible; one-at-a-time effects remain non-additive and do not establish live prevalence.
learnings.apply_when: Interpreting or simplifying the ORF candidate-structure mechanism after public synthetic validation.

learnings.lesson: A global design/config freeze and a per-family prediction freeze are different evidence events; whole-phase prospective wording is valid only when all family predictions precede every family result.
learnings.apply_when: A Phase-4/6 report summarizes sequential experiment-family preregistration or freeze chronology.

learnings.lesson: A literature freshness search must identify the conceptual owner of the estimand and the operational owner of the missing step before surveying recent application neighbors.
learnings.apply_when: A Phase-1 literature map positions novelty for an application-specific instantiation of a standard decision quantity.

learnings.lesson: State validation must reject new unstructured learnings and failure_class values outside the allowed enum while reporting legacy violations without rewriting history.
learnings.apply_when: ORIENT or RECORD validates state.json after historical schema evolution.

learnings.lesson: A self-hashed manifest proves internal consistency, not common identity or authenticity; pair protocols need an exact schema, an external trust root, and one digest pinned across every child and final envelope.
learnings.apply_when: A Phase-2/3 multi-process protocol uses a manifest to claim all runs share one authenticated execution environment.

learnings.lesson: Callable-entry bytes are not authenticated output unless fixture-controlled storage emits them directly or the complete post-capture writer/result path is source-bound.
learnings.apply_when: A Phase-2/3 framework correspondence claim observes callable input through a later framework return value.

learnings.lesson: When a gate concept is already occupied, endpoint artifacts and aggregate regression tables cannot support a novel longitudinal safety claim; identifiability requires every accepted and rejected candidate joined to its diff, security and utility measurements, decision, and immutable verifier identity.
learnings.apply_when: A Phase-1/2 self-evolution study proposes to measure security debt or the effect of candidate acceptance using published harness artifacts.

learnings.lesson: A one-sample wall-clock race across several fast mock arms is not a stable bottleneck profile; host jitter plus winner selection can reverse a thresholded routing decision even when code and seeds are unchanged.
learnings.apply_when: A Phase-2 engineering hypothesis uses sub-second wall-clock mocks or selects the fastest template/arm before comparing a derived rate.

learnings.lesson: Generation cost measured on a reused attack environment omits the evaluator's fresh environment/agent construction per replay candidate; candidate multiplicity can amortize this hidden replay-only fixed term even when agent action latency is linear.
learnings.apply_when: A competition allocator projects replay capacity from attack-time reset/interact measurements or compares candidate message multiplicities.

learnings.lesson: Capping an aggregate event count by the number of requested messages does not estimate message-level coverage; each credited event must be attributed to its requested message or unique marker before an arm is admitted.
learnings.apply_when: A Phase-2/3 multi-message selector uses tool-event counts as a coverage or firing-rate gate.
